correctness.rationale: The tensor-amplification theorem checks. Compressing a quasidiagonal approximation by the spectral projection of a tensor-factor projection produces a quasidiagonal conditional trace on the remaining factor. Repeating this along cube edges forces every word-sector projection to have mass \(2^{-r}\). The product quasidiagonal trace is the equal convex combination of the sector traces; testing against \(2E_\omega-1\) gives the lower norm bound, while orthogonal support of the complementary convex combination gives equality. Amenability of each sector trace follows because amenable traces form a face. On the inductive-limit tensor power, finite-stage restrictions give lower bounds tending to two, while product-state finite-stage approximations give the amenable and quasidiagonal infinite product traces. Moradi's full primary paper verifies exactly the required base assumptions: Lemma 3.2 supplies the two sector traces and equal quasidiagonal midpoint, and Theorem 4.1 forces every quasidiagonal trace to assign sector mass one half.
risks: The infinite tensor power is not claimed to remain residually finite dimensional.
No exactness, nuclearity, UCT, or simplicity conclusion is used.
